violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. An employee was cooking batches of raw beef on the griddle while wearing gloves. The PIC stated the employee changes gloves after touching the raw beef and before touching the cooked beef, but did not indicate that the employee washes hands before putting on new gloves.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. The EHS educated the PIC on how the employee must wash hands before putting on new gloves and then educated her staff on this.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Cleanser, Availability
violations.observation: Observed that hand soap was not provided at each handwashing sink. There was no soap available at the hand sink.
violations.corrective_action: Provide hand soap at each hand sink to allow employees to properly wash their hands. The PIC corrected this during the inspection. TAQUERIA CANCUN (Inspection Date: 07/14/2026) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: Access to Handwashing Sink
violations.observation: The handwashing facility located on the cook line is blocked by a prep table placed right next to it, preventing access by employees for easy handwashing. When an employee is working at the prep table, other employees can’t access the hand sink and it’s the only hand sink in the establishment.
violations.corrective_action: A hand washing sink shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for employee use. Please relocate or remove the prep table so that the hand sink is always accessible. It is very important that employee always be able to wash their hands. The EHS discussed this with the PIC, who said they understood and would look into relocating the prep table to make the hand sink more accessible. This violation needs to be corrected as soon as possible, or within 10 days. A follow-up inspection is scheduled for Friday, July 24, 2026. Please have the table moved by then.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: observed raw chicken store over raw beef in the walk- in in two separate locations.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). The PIC corrected this during the inspection.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: a large container of birria beef in one of the prep refrigerators was not date-marked. Several quart containers of thawed soups were not date-marked. All items are held more than 24 hours. Most other foods were properly date-marked.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. Ensure that all TCS foods prepared on site and held more than 24 hours are date-marked. The PIC date-marked the items above during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Separation of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. The sanitizer bucket for the wiping cloths was stored on the food counter where cherries, raw beef and other foods were being prepped.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored to prevent contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items by separating the poisonous and toxic materials by spacing or partitioning. The PIC moved the solution during the inspection to an appropriate location to correct.

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: Observed frozen vacuum packed tilapia being thawed improperly without opening the vacuum packed packaging.
violations.corrective_action: When thawing vacuum packed fish, always cut the bags open to let in oxygen. There is bacteria that lives and grows in vacuum packed foods, cutting the bags open and exposing the bacteria to oxygen kills it. The EHS educated the PIC on this requirement. The PIC cut the thawing fish packages open during the inspection to correct.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Food Storage No Contamination
violations.observation: Food stored in a location where it is subject to splash, dust or other contamination as follows: an employee was preparing single service containers of condiments for take out orders and the table she was preparing these on was directly next to the handsink, exposing the food to possible contamination from employees washing their hands.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food where it is not exposed to splash, dust or other contamination. As stated in another violation, the prep table should not be right next to the hand sink because when employee are working on it, the hand sink is not accessible, and the table should be moved. The table should also be moved because when employees are washing their hands, the food being prepared on the table is exposed to contamination. Move the table away from the hand sink. The EHS discussed this with the PIC. Correct as soon as possible or before the next routine inspection, not to exceed 6 months.

out_items.name: Utensils, equipment and linens properly stored, dried and handled

violations.title: Equip/Utensils/Linens Stored off Floor, Clean Location
violations.observation: Observed white 5-gallon buckets stored in the hand sink. These buckets appeared to be clean.
violations.corrective_action: Cleaned equipment and utensils, laundered linens, and single-service items shall be stored in a clean, dry location where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches off the floor on NSF approved shelving units or dunnage racks. Discontinue storing any equipment used for food in the mop sink.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. The manager could not locate the vomit and diarrhea clean up policy.
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. The environmental health specialist (EHS) provided the manager with a copy of the Fairfax County Health Dept. model policy to implement.CDI.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: observed raw chicken stored over salsa in the walk-in.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The manager corrected this by moving the chicken to another shelf. CDI.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal Foods Different Types
violations.observation: Different types of raw animal foods stored in such a manner that may cause cross contamination as follows: Observed raw chicken stored over raw beef in the walk-in.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods shall be sorted by their 'type' and cooking temperatures while in storage inside a refrigerator or freezer. For example, if using ONE shelving unit for storage of ONLY raw foods, the foods shall be sorted in this manner: 1) raw poultry (chicken, turkey, or duck) shall be stored on the BOTTOM shelf (165F cook temperature), 2) raw ground beef and ground pork shall be stored on the shelf above poultry (155F cook temperature), and 3) raw pork (chops, ribs), seafood, and shell eggs shall be stored on the top shelf above beef (145F cook temperature). The manager corrected this by changing the locations of the foods.

violations.title: Cooking Raw Animal Foods, Minimum of 165F
violations.observation: The following poultry item was not cooked to a sufficient temperature and/or time to eliminate pathogenic bacteria: raw chicken was cooked to 155º F during the inspection.
violations.corrective_action: Raw animal foods such as poultry, wild game animals, stuffed fish, stuffed meat, stuffed pasta, stuffed poultry, stuffed ratites, or stuffing containing any of these raw animal foods shall be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 165F for at least 15 seconds. The manager had the food employee reheat the chicken to 167º F to correct. CDI.

violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw beef over RTE cut tomatoes for pico de gallo in the WIR.

Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. CFM re-arranged order.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food, Disposition
violations.observation: Observed the following ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food being held for more than the specified time/temperature allowed: beef birria broth dated 07/10/25.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be discarded if it: 1) exceeds 7 days or at 41F (except the time it is frozen); or 2) is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day. Item discarded.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: raw shrimp thawing in standing water.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. Education provided.

out_items.name: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean

violations.title: Physical Facilities, Maintain Good Repair
violations.observation: Observed that the ceiling in the back kitchen area is not maintained in good repair.
violations.corrective_action: Repair the physical facilities. Poor repair and maintenance compromises the functionality of the physical facilities.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: OBSERVATION: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.'
violations.corrective_action: CORRECTIVE ACTION: Provided manager Employee Health Policy documents in Spanish. Training to be provided to staff and signatures obtained. A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. Handouts are available in the following languages: English, Arabic, Chinese (traditional), Farsi, Hindi, Korean, Spanish, Thai, Urdu and Vietnamese. If you have any questions about your employee health policy, please contact your area inspector or contact the Health Department at 703- 246-2201, TTY 703-591-6435.
